A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 23-page versions of the same MSWT paper. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison; pages 3–22 are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original model evaluations on chaotic Kolmogorov flow (CKF), shallow water equations (SWE) and ERA5, including rollout errors, spectra and climatology metrics.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds component-ablation results on CKF in Appendix B.5 and Table 9.

M1.justification: The proposed MSWT architecture, objectives and inference procedure in Sections 3–4 remain unchanged. Appendix B.5 introduces experimental ablation variants rather than revising the proposed model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CKF, SWE and ERA5. The new ablations reuse the existing CKF rollout task without adding datasets, populations or input-environment scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds three internal comparators: MSWT-V1 with patch size 1, MSWT-V2 without attention, and MSWT-V3 with convolutional sampling. Participation of the existing external baselines remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.5 adds controlled CKF configurations using patch size 1, attention removal, and stride-2 convolution/deconvolution replacements. These are evaluated with the existing Rel L2, EMLR and EMAE metrics at steps 1, 30 and 64. Previously reported protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 examines patch-size sensitivity in Section 5.4 and Table 6. v2 adds dedicated ablations of all three central modules—tokenization, wavelet attention and wavelet-preserving sampling—with accuracy and training-time comparisons in Table 9. This substantially expands direct validation of component contributions.

E5.justification: Existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and the five-seed ERA5 evaluations are unchanged. Table 9 supplies point estimates, as Table 6 already did, without introducing run counts, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds CKF ablation outcomes: step-64 Rel L2 is 0.35 for MSWT, 0.18 for V1, 1.09 for V2 and 0.71 for V3, alongside enstrophy errors and training times. Tables 1–8 remain unchanged, including Table 1's MSWT value of 0.33 ± 0.03; the new reference score is not a correction to that retained result.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, equations 1–43 and Appendix A's wavelet definitions and derivations are unchanged. The new ablation section introduces no formal assumptions, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about spectral fidelity, efficiency, long-horizon stability and ERA5 climatological accuracy.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 interprets the ablations as support for wavelet attention and wavelet-preserving sampling. It also identifies an accuracy–efficiency tradeoff: eliminating patch aggregation improves accuracy while increasing training time. These component-specific interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents the ablation constructions, including pointwise mapping with patch size 1 and stride-2 sampling replacements. Table 9 newly reports training times: 1h17m for MSWT, 3h4m for V1, 35m for V2 and 1h4m for V3. Existing implementation and access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and bibliography are unchanged. Appendix B.5 adds no citations or revised positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 appends the short B.5 subsection with variant descriptions and interpretation. It also changes the corresponding author from Xuesong Wang to Edwin V. Bonilla and updates date/version text. Existing scientific prose and section ordering are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9 and moves the unchanged Figure 20 upward on the final page to accommodate Appendix B.5. The revised correspondence footnote causes limited reflow on pages 1–2; other figures, tables and page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.5 strengthens the empirical basis for the architecture by testing all three central components, extending v1's patch-size sensitivity analysis and exposing the tokenizer's accuracy–runtime tradeoff. The improvement is limited: the tests cover only CKF, lack uncertainty and run-count reporting, and do not explain their differing full-model reference scores relative to Table 1.
